meta.title: Summa: study with your PDFs and a tutor
meta.description: Study with your PDFs and a tutor that won’t give you the answer before you do. Free and open source, for macOS, Windows and Linux.

features.title: What’s on the desk
features.readersText: Search, outline and bookmarks. The tutor cites “File.pdf, p. N” and a click opens the page.
features.checkText: Sends your handwritten page to the tutor. No computer nearby? A QR code takes the photos.
features.pdfsText: Problem list, handout, summary, mock exam and formula sheet, with an A4 preview before saving.
features.notebookText: What you saved comes back in Review today.
features.figuresText: Charts and activities in the chat, offline. GeoGebra when you need it.
features.miniText: The conversation in a small window, always on top of Xournal++.
out.label: Privacy and models
out.localText: PDFs, conversations and notebook live in a folder of yours. No cloud account.
out.telemetryText: Summa sends nothing about you anywhere.
out.modelsText: Starts with OpenCode’s free models. Another provider’s account signs in inside the app.
faq.title: Questions
faq.costText: Nothing. Summa is open source, under the MIT license. OpenCode’s free models work without a card; if you already pay a provider, its account signs in inside the app.
faq.answer: Does the tutor give me the answer?
faq.answerText: Not before you try. It points to where the mistake is, cites the page of your material and hands the question back. The right answer only shows up after yours.
faq.xournalText: No. Check captures the window of any writing app, and the phone photo covers paper notebooks. Ambitus, the version of Xournal++ made for Summa, sends the page directly.
faq.cloud: Do my PDFs go to the cloud?
faq.cloudText: Your files stay in your folder. To answer, the tutor reads the pages it needs and sends that excerpt to the model you chose, as in any AI chat.
faq.os: Which systems does it run on?
faq.osText: macOS, Windows and Linux (AppImage). On Linux, Check works with Ambitus.
faq.offlineText: The readers, Notebook, calculator and chat figures do. The tutor needs the internet to talk to the model.
faq.warning: Why does my system warn me the first time?
faq.warningText: Summa doesn’t have an Apple or Microsoft certificate yet, so macOS and Windows warn you once. The steps for each are under Install. After that, updates arrive signed through About → Update.
faq.modelsText: Yes. OpenCode changes its free list from time to time, and a model may leave or start charging. Summa’s picker shows the ones that are live and the data policy of each; if yours leaves, pick another there.
faq.langText: English and Portuguese, in the interface and the tutor. Switch in Settings.
install.title: Install
install.mac2: Open the image and drag Summa to Applications.
install.mac3: On first launch, follow the note beside this.
install.macNote: “Summa Not Opened”? Click Done, then go to System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. Only once.
install.win2: Open the file. No administrator needed.
install.winNote: “Windows protected your PC”? Click More info, then Run anyway. Only once. If the Visual C++ Redistributable x64 is missing, Summa shows the link.
install.linux2: Make it executable and open it. The menu shortcut appears on its own.
